newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Wms de Broe aims for more Lithuania involvement.
newsitem.headline: Wms de Broe aims for more Lithuania involvement.

text.p: Williams de Broe aims to become one of the most active investors in Lithuania's financial markets, taking part in privatisation and equity market investments, the bank told daily Lietuvos rytas on Monday.

"We are interested in nearly all the sectors of Lithuania's economy, energy projects and privatisation of state-owned companies," Williams de Broe official Petri Karjalainen told the newspaper in an interview.
"Our bank has already become one of the most active market participants in Estonia and will seek for the same in Lithuania", Karjalainen added.
Williams de Broe is majority-owned by Belgium's Banque Bruxelles Lambert SA (BBL) and Karjalainen is head of its Baltic states division, based in Helsinki.
The newspaper said Williams de Broe would help privatise state industries, seek strategic partners and be an intermediary in issuing global depositary receipts (GDRs).

Karjalainen said the bank was continuing talks with several firms although he would not say which. The newspaper said Williams de Broe was interested in light industry, textiles, milk processing and the transport and energy sectors.
Karjalainen would not say how many firms the bank would carry out GDR issues for but said it would be less than 10.
"It is necessary to privatise big companies on the international market since there is simply not enough capital in Lithuania," Karjalainen added.
De Broe recently bought a stake in Lithuanian cheese maker Rokisko and has also been active in the northernmost Baltic state, Estonia.
